I am a 57-year-old farmer in Huaiqiao Township, Xizhangtou Village, Quzhou County. I have been farming these 14 mu for 25 years since I finished middle school. My wife and I work the land together. Our two children have jobs in town — one makes 36,000 yuan a year and the other 18,000 — so they send money home, but they cannot help much during the busy season. We rely on our well for irrigation, which is reliable but costs electricity.

My farm is organized around four crops. I started growing stevia five years ago when the cooperative introduced it. It is my best-paying crop, so I treat it as my main business. I keep 2 mu for stevia. I also maintain 1 mu of cotton because I have decades of experience with it and the buyers still come to the village, even though it demands a lot of labor for spraying. The remaining 11 mu is my wheat-maize rotation — this is my foundation. I planted the winter wheat last October, and it is in the field now. As soon as I harvest the wheat around May 25, I will plant maize on that same land.

It is spring now, so this is how I will manage each crop this year:

For my **stevia** on 2 mu, I will transplant seedlings around April 2. I prepare the land with rotary tillage because stevia needs loose soil for the roots. I will lay plastic film mulch to keep the soil warm and moist. Stevia is a leafy crop that needs a lot of nutrients and water, so I apply compound fertilizer three times — once as basal and twice as topdressing — and I will irrigate seven times through the season. I also need to spray insecticide five times and herbicide once to keep the leaves clean for the buyer. I expect about 250 kg per mu.

For my **cotton** on 1 mu, I will sow Jinmian 4 around April 5 with plastic film mulch. I use no-tillage for cotton to save labor and preserve soil moisture. I apply one basal compound fertilizer and that is enough for the whole season. The big challenge with cotton is pests — I will spray insecticide thirteen times and herbicide once, plus use plant growth regulators twice to control height. I only irrigate once because summer rain usually helps, and I harvest in late October. I expect about 300 kg per mu of seed cotton.

For my **wheat** on 11 mu, it is already growing in the field. I planted Luyuan 502 last October with rotary tillage. Now in spring, I need to topdress once with compound fertilizer and irrigate three more times before harvest around May 25. I spray insecticide once and herbicide once — that is enough if you catch the weeds early. I expect about 600 kg per mu. I keep some for family consumption and sell the rest.

For my **maize** on the same 11 mu, I will sow Denghai 662 hybrid seed right after wheat harvest around June 2. I use no-tillage direct seeding — there is no time to plow between wheat harvest and maize sowing, and the hybrid performs well this way. I apply compound fertilizer at planting plus urea at topdressing once, irrigate three times, and spray insecticide three times, herbicide once, and regulator once. I harvest around October 1. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

This plan is what I know works on my land. The stevia and cotton give me cash income, while the wheat-maize rotation feeds my family and provides stable grain sales.
